## Review guide

This PR adds tokenization reuse for text chat sessions. Two optional follow-ups are described separately in my fork: [block-hash reuse](https://github.com/RichealYoung/vllm/blob/54891283404c5814970523c9acc44f85b8104067/pr63361/v2/README.md) and [image compatibility](https://github.com/RichealYoung/vllm/blob/54891283404c5814970523c9acc44f85b8104067/pr63361/v3/README.md). Each page links to its incremental code.
If you prefer reviewing everything together or as stacked PRs, I can switch.

## Overview

Successive chat turns often resend a long conversation with only a small addition. This PR avoids tokenizing the unchanged text again by retaining the previous rendered prompt and token IDs for each session. Clients continue to send complete requests; an agent hint—the existing `session_id` field—selects the previous prompt to compare, and text comparison determines what can be reused. See [RFC #63359](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63359).

## Claims

- Opt-in reuse of tokenized text across session turns, with a configurable CPU memory budget; disabled by default.
- In a synthetic replay of growing chat histories, frontend CPU time per request decreased **25.1%** and mean time to first output decreased **19.7%** across four pairs of runs. End-to-end request latency decreased about **1.0%**. Short independent requests did not show a consistent benefit.

## Validation

Qwen3-0.6B on an RTX 3090, FP16, four concurrent clients, with prefix caching, chunked prefill and CUDA graphs enabled. For each workload, each configuration is tested in four fresh-server runs of 80 requests. The memory budget for cached text and token IDs is 512 MiB.

| Metric | Baseline | Token reuse | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Growing histories: frontend CPU time/request | 389.5 CPU-ms | 291.7 CPU-ms | −25.1% |
| Growing histories: mean time to first output | 641.1 ms | 515.3 ms | −19.7%; individual runs −27.0% to −2.2% |
| Growing histories: mean end-to-end latency | 8.391 s | 8.306 s | approximately −1.0% |
| Independent requests: mean time to first output | 99.7 ms | 98.0 ms | individual runs −9.5% to +10.9% |
| Independent requests: P95 time to first output | 133.9 ms | 137.1 ms | tail latency increased |

Growing histories contain 16K–35K input tokens and generate 448 tokens; independent requests contain 512/1024/2048 input tokens and generate 64 tokens. Time to first output is measured at the client, from request start to the first non-empty streamed output chunk. CPU time/request is the CPU time used by the API server process divided by request count. Percentages average the relative changes between matched baseline and reuse runs; P95 values average the four run P95s.

Clients send their next request when the previous response finishes. Latency gains varied substantially between runs and should not be assumed for other arrival patterns. Reported prefix-cache hit token counts matched request by request between configurations.

Validation performed by the author: **371 CPU tests**, applicable pre-commit checks, and **36 requests to running Qwen3 and Llama servers** with reuse enabled and disabled.

The performance results above were measured before the latest commit, [04d5f00e8](https://github.com/RichealYoung/vllm/commit/04d5f00e8bf6836c3a4ead37e9ec7dc04ec68ee8), and were not rerun. That commit only lowers the cost of memory accounting; in a CPU component measurement, prefix-hit encoding took about 0.8 ms less per request.

<details>
<summary>Test coverage and reproduction details</summary>

The tests compare runs with reuse enabled and disabled, checking complete prompt token IDs, reported token counts and generated outputs. They also confirm that both whole-prompt and prefix reuse occur. CPU tests cover tokenizer compatibility checks, edited histories, cache memory limits, requests sharing cached entries, cancellation, reset and normal processing of requests containing media.

After updating to main, the existing reasoning/render-parity and CLI checks passed 19 cases each on main and the candidate. A deliberately broken mapping failed the new regression test. [Source identity and regression evidence](https://github.com/RichealYoung/vllm/blob/fc4a884d5af411c72cf290578a4ed1441f3770dd/pr63361/v1/main-update-20261026/README.md) include the commands, logs and results. The latest commit, which charges only newly tokenized IDs and tolerates leftover truncation/padding tokenizer state, passed the same checks with 3 added tests: [accounting update evidence](https://github.com/RichealYoung/vllm/blob/a36f03e3f27476dbfe9a0914fa9b8775f89d1093/pr63361/v1/accounting-update-20261030/README.md).

To run the CPU tests, install the repository test dependencies and use:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/utils_/test_session_prefix.py \
  tests/renderers/test_session_prefix.py \
  tests/renderers/test_session_prefix_media_fallback.py \
  tests/v1/test_request.py \
  tests/config/test_config_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py
```

To run the serving tests, also obtain the Qwen3 and Llama model files and use:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  -k test_session_prefix_text_requests_preserve_native_ids_and_outputs
```

These performance measurements use the earlier frozen source; they were not rerun after the update to main.

The benchmark uses a maximum model length of 40,960, up to four sequences, 4,096 batched tokens and 18 GiB of KV cache. Sampling uses temperature 0, seed 42, fixed output lengths and thinking disabled. Each fresh server receives eight warmup requests without session IDs, followed by a prefix-cache reset before measurement. Server and client are pinned to different logical CPUs. Both builds use base `be08fa535` with the same benchmark patch applied.

The [fixed benchmark inputs, raw results and replay scripts](https://github.com/RichealYoung/vllm/blob/5e4c5f82c146fa8f238b1af5baf3c6527a53d4ba/pr63361/performance/REPRODUCTION.md) include source revisions, build details, the patch applied to both builds, full server arguments and per-run records.

</details>

## Details

### How it works

After applying the chat template, compare the prompt with the previous prompt in the same session. Reuse cached token IDs up to a safe tokenizer boundary within their common prefix, and tokenize only the remaining suffix. To locate it, scan backward for an added token (such as a chat delimiter) whose matching rules allow independent tokenization on either side, then verify its position against the cached token IDs. If no safe boundary exists, use normal tokenization.

### Usage and limits

Enable with `--session-token-cache-mb <MiB>` and send the existing `session_id` field or `X-Session-ID` header. Each renderer stores one previous prompt for each session and `cache_salt` value.

<details>
<summary>Usage example and tokenizer compatibility</summary>

Start a server with a 32 MiB budget for cached text and token IDs per renderer:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --tokenizer-revision c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca \
  --session-token-cache-mb 32
```

Send the same session ID with successive complete chat histories:

```json
{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
  "session_id": "conversation-123",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "..."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "..."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "..."}
  ]
}
```

The default budget is zero, which disables reuse. Tested library combinations are Transformers 5.16.1, 5.17.0, 5.18.0, 5.19.0, 5.20.0, 5.20.1 or 5.20.2 with tokenizers 0.23.2 or 0.23.3. The tokenizer backend configuration and encoding implementation must also match a supported configuration; a library version or model name alone is insufficient. The feature documentation in this PR lists the tested tokenizers and revisions. Requests containing media use normal tokenization.

</details>

The history memory limit covers stored entries, space reserved for pending entries, and entries still in use; it does not cap total process memory. Cancellation, failures and resets prevent incomplete or outdated entries from being cached.

Short prompts, frequent edits, conversations that branch from earlier turns, and requests routed between processes can reduce reuse or make its overhead outweigh the savings.

Related frontend work: [#47583](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47583), [#45514](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45514), [#61335](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61335). The agent hint selects one previous prompt from the same session for comparison.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

+def test_lcp_matches_character_scan():
+    def reference(a, b):
+        i = 0
+        while i < min(len(a), len(b)) and a[i] == b[i]:
+            i += 1
+        return i
+
+    rng = random.Random(0)
+    alphabet = "ab<>中文🙂é"
+    cases = [("", ""), ("", "a"), ("abc", "abc"), ("abc", "abx"), ("abc", "ab")]
+    cases.append(("🙂éa", "🙂éb"))
+    long_text = "中文🙂é" * 4096
+    cases.extend((long_text, long_text[:i] + "x") for i in (0, 1, 8192, len(long_text)))
+    for _ in range(500):
+        a = "".join(rng.choices(alphabet, k=rng.randrange(40)))
+        b = a[: rng.randrange(len(a) + 1)] + "".join(
+            rng.choices(alphabet, k=rng.randrange(10))
+        )
+        cases.append((a, b))
+    for a, b in cases:
+        assert lcp(a, b) == lcp(b, a) == reference(a, b)

+def test_token_accounting_never_understates_owned_list_and_elements():
+    class IntSubclass(int):
+        pass
+
+    rng = random.Random(42)
+    for ids in (
+        [],
+        [0, 0, 1, 151669],
+        [0, (1 << 30) - 1, 1 << 30, (1 << 32) - 1],
+        [-1, 1],
+        [1 << 32, 1 << 300],
+        [IntSubclass(7), True, 9],
+        [rng.randrange(151670) for _ in range(1024)],
+    ):
+        reference = (
+            sys.getsizeof([])
+            + len(ids) * struct.calcsize("P")
+            + sum(map(sys.getsizeof, ids))
+        )
+        assert token_bytes(ids) >= reference
+        if all(type(i) is int and 0 <= i < (1 << 30) for i in ids):
+            assert token_bytes(ids) == reference

+def test_validated_bound_matches_full_scan_accounting():
+    """A bound from validated parts charges what a full scan would."""
+
+    class IntSubclass(int):
+        pass
+
+    rng = random.Random(7)
+    prefix = [rng.randrange(151670) for _ in range(512)]
+    suffix = [rng.randrange(151670) for _ in range(64)]
+    combined = prefix + suffix
+    prefix_bound, suffix_bound = token_bound(prefix), token_bound(suffix)
+    assert prefix_bound is not None and suffix_bound is not None
+    bound = max(prefix_bound, suffix_bound)
+    assert bound == token_bound(combined)
+    assert token_bytes(combined, bound) == token_bytes(combined)
+    # An upper bound from a longer validated snapshot may only overstate.
+    assert token_bytes(prefix[:100], token_bound(prefix)) >= token_bytes(prefix[:100])
+    for invalid in ([True, 0], [IntSubclass(7)], [-1], [1 << 32], (1, 2), [1.0]):
+        assert token_bound(cast(list[int], invalid)) is None

+    store = SessionPrefixStore[str](100)

+def test_concurrent_requests_publish_in_completion_order():
+    store = SessionPrefixStore[str](100)

+    def b():

+"""Bounded process-local candidate snapshots, including in-flight readers."""
+
+import struct
+import sys
+import threading
+from collections import OrderedDict
+from collections.abc import Hashable, Iterator
+from contextlib import contextmanager

+from typing import Generic, TypeVar
+

+
+
+def lcp(a: str, b: str) -> int:
+    """Exact common prefix length; slice comparisons run in CPython's C code."""
+    n = min(len(a), len(b))
+    if a[:n] == b[:n]:
+        return n
+    lo, hi = 0, n  # a[:lo] == b[:lo] and a[:hi] != b[:hi]
+    while hi - lo > 1:
+        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
+        if a[lo:mid] == b[lo:mid]:
+            lo = mid
+        else:
+            hi = mid
+    return lo
+
+
+def token_bound(ids: list[int]) -> int | None:
+    """Largest ID if ``ids`` is an exact list of exact uint32 ints, else None."""
+    if (
+        sys.implementation.name == "cpython"
+        and type(ids) is list
+        and not (set(map(type, ids)) - {int})
+    ):
+        maximum = max(ids, default=0)
+        if min(ids, default=0) >= 0 and maximum <= 0xFFFFFFFF:
+            return maximum
+    return None
+

+def token_bytes(ids: list[int], bound: int | None = None) -> int:
+    """Bytes owned by ``ids`` and its elements, never understated.
+
+    ``bound`` may be passed only when every element of the exact list ``ids``
+    is already known to be an exact uint32 int no larger than it, e.g. the
+    maximum of validated parts; otherwise the list is scanned.
+    """
+    if bound is None:
+        bound = token_bound(ids)
+    if bound is not None:
+        # Count every occurrence, including shared integer objects.
+        return sys.getsizeof([]) + len(ids) * (
+            struct.calcsize("P") + sys.getsizeof(bound)
+        )
+    return (
+        sys.getsizeof([])
+        + len(ids) * struct.calcsize("P")
+        + sum(map(sys.getsizeof, ids))
+    )

+class _Entry(Generic[_T]):
+    value: _T
+    size: int

+    def __init__(self, store: "SessionPrefixStore[_T]", key: Hashable, size: int):

+    """

+            raise ValueError("session history capacity must be nonnegative")

+        self.bytes_used = 0
+        self.epoch = 0
+        self.closed = False
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()

+        entry.resident = False
+        if not entry.readers:
+            self.bytes_used -= entry.size

+        with self._lock:
+            entry = self._entries.get(key)
+            if entry is not None:
+                entry.readers += 1
+                self._entries.move_to_end(key)

+            yield entry.value if entry is not None else None
+        finally:
+            if entry is not None:
+                with self._lock:
+                    entry.readers -= 1
+                    if not entry.resident and not entry.readers:
+                        self.bytes_used -= entry.size
+
+    def reserve(self, key: Hashable, size: int) -> Reservation[_T] | None:
+        retired = []
+        with self._lock:
+            if self.closed or size <= 0 or size > self.capacity:
+                return None
+            while self.bytes_used + size > self.capacity and self._entries:
+                _, entry = self._entries.popitem(last=False)
+                self._retire(entry)
+                retired.append(entry)
+            if self.bytes_used + size > self.capacity:
+                return None
+            self.bytes_used += size
+            result = Reservation(self, key, size)
+        return result

+    def clear(self, *, close: bool = False) -> None:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.epoch += 1
+            self.closed |= close

+            for entry in entries.values():
+                self._retire(entry)

+    key: tuple[str | None, str]
+    epoch: int
+    pending: tuple[Reservation, object, int] | None = None
+    active: bool = True
+    _lock: threading.Lock = field(default_factory=threading.Lock, repr=False)

+        with self._lock:
+            self.active = False
+            pending, self.pending = self.pending, None
+        if pending is not None:
+            reservation, value, size = pending
